scope: One focused primary checkout contract run for the manual coverage workflow. It verifies coverage-job-only branch-capable tooling, lock-derived Vitest provider installation and runtime matching, and fail-closed Rust LCOV branch-observation semantics. It does not generate global coverage, run on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu, update a ratchet baseline, or establish a coverage percentage.

application.sourceSnapshotQualification: manual-validation.yml is outside SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_PATHS, so this focused report binds its configuration files explicitly and is not a whole-source snapshot claim.

coverageConfiguration.ordinaryRustLanes: full-source, fuzz, and provider-smoke remain configured for Rust 1.89.0
coverageConfiguration.vitestCoverageProvider: The workflow derives the provider version from package-lock.json node_modules/vitest, installs it with --ignore-scripts --no-save --package-lock=false --no-audit, and checks installed Vitest and coverage-provider versions against that value before coverage generation.
coverageConfiguration.branchAvailabilityGate: The workflow reads coverage/rust.lcov through summarizeLcov and coverageAvailability and fails with a fixed error when Rust branches are unavailable. It does not turn zero observations into 100 percent.
coverageConfiguration.artifactRetention: The coverage artifact upload uses if: always() to retain any generated partial report while a failed generation or branch-availability check still fails the job.

semanticBranchFixtures.observed: The contract extracts and executes the workflow heredoc against a temporary LCOV fixture containing BRDA data and succeeds.
semanticBranchFixtures.unavailable: The same extracted workflow check rejects a temporary LCOV fixture with no BRDA records and requires the fixed unavailable-branch error.

sensitivity: Removing --branch from the Rust LCOV command made the contract fail.
Replacing the lock-derived coverage provider with 4.1.10 made the contract fail.
Changing the fuzz lane from Rust 1.89.0 to 1.88.0 made the contract fail.
Moving the installed Vitest runtime check after coverage generation made the contract fail.
Removing the post-LCOV branch-observation check made the contract fail.
Removing if: always() from coverage artifact upload made the contract fail.
formatAndPatchChecks: Prettier passed for both changed files.
git apply --check --whitespace=error-all passed for the reviewed patch.

limitations: No GitHub-hosted Ubuntu coverage job ran, so nightly installation, networked npm installation, and full workspace LCOV generation remain unexecuted.
No actual global Rust or frontend coverage report, branch percentage, or ratchet comparison is recorded here.
The branch-availability gate requires observed Rust branch records but sets no percentage threshold.
This is configuration and focused contract evidence only; it does not establish native, provider, release, performance, fuzzing, or dependency-audit acceptance.
